code_review.project_type: web application — FastAPI REST backend + React 19 SPA monorepo (gallery of seven AI example apps)

existing_self_description.text: Built with Spec4 (BWS4) is a living showcase of common AI application patterns, presented as a collection of small, self-contained example apps behind a single landing page. Each example demonstrates one pattern end-to-end: how it's built, what it depends on, and how it behaves, so that visitors unfamiliar with the underlying technique can understand it by seeing it work rather than by reading about it abstractly.

architecture.summary: Layered modular monolith with per-example vertical slices: each example app (embeddings, single_call, rag, tools, chained_calls, planning, orchestrated) owns a backend package with schemas.py, service.py and versioned Markdown prompts, exposed through deliberately thin FastAPI routers in backend/app/api/, while cross-cutting capabilities (generation, agent_runtime, model_registry, embedding, moderation, text_gate, web_search, storage, allowance_holds) live in backend/app/services/ and are reused by every slice. The React SPA mirrors this with route-based code-splitting, one lazy chunk per example app.

incomplete_or_dead_code: `uv run ruff check .` covers only code written from v5 onward: pyproject.toml's extend-exclude list exempts backend/app/main.py, api/, chained_calls/, core/, db/, embeddings/, planning/, rag/, single_call/, tools/, ten individually named services/*.py files and several test paths, where the manifest comment records 366 unfixed ruff findings across 57 files — a clean lint run does not mean the touched files were linted.

No typecheck invocation is documented anywhere despite mypy>=2.3.0 being a declared dev dependency; there is no Makefile, script alias, or README command for it, so mypy is installed but not wired into any workflow.
No CI workflow exists, so the pytest/ruff/vitest gates are only ever run manually.

README claims the embeddings plot ships only the ~1 MB `plotly-basic` build, but frontend/package.json depends on the full `plotly.js@^3.7.0`; the size claim holds only if the embeddings route imports the basic bundle explicitly — verify before touching that route.
backend/tests/golden/planning_cases.json exists but no corresponding planning test module appears in the tests listing, so the planning slice may be untested against its own golden cases.

change_risks.risk: README states the per-capability chains 'both rot as providers retire free slugs'; code that assumes a specific model slug will fail unpredictably as providers withdraw free models
change_risks.mitigation_hint: always resolve models through the registry's ordered fallback chain and bench list; never hard-code a provider slug in an example app

change_risks.area: two model lanes (LiteLLM in services/generation.py, PydanticAI in services/agent_runtime.py)
change_risks.risk: both lanes must read slugs from model_registry and pass the same usage-limit gate; new code that calls a provider SDK directly silently escapes quota accounting and the shared free-tier caps
change_risks.mitigation_hint: route every new model call through the registry plus the allowance/usage-limit gate, mirroring agent_runtime.py

change_risks.risk: ensure_built() failures are caught and only logged by design, so a broken embeddings projection surfaces as a slow or failing first request rather than a boot failure; Render free-tier spin-down (~15 min idle) makes cold start a routine path, not an edge case
change_risks.mitigation_hint: assert on the embeddings_projection_warmup_failed log and on first-request latency, not just on process start

change_risks.risk: README documents that 2 of the 8 free models do not honour a JSON Schema directive and that nonconformance is reported with raw output on purpose; relaxing validation to make tests green would erase the behaviour the example exists to show
change_risks.mitigation_hint: treat nonconforming responses as an expected, displayed outcome rather than a bug to suppress

change_risks.risk: migrations assume the pgvector extension can be enabled; a non-Neon or restricted Postgres will fail at the first revision and the RAG example's HNSW index cannot be created
change_risks.mitigation_hint: verify `CREATE EXTENSION vector` privileges on the target database before running alembic upgrade head

change_risks.risk: a failed second call returns HTTP 200 with status 'critique_failed' deliberately so the surviving first-call output reaches the client; changing it to a 4xx/5xx would push the client's error branch and discard the story
change_risks.mitigation_hint: preserve the 200-with-status contract; only failures leaving nothing to show are error statuses

security_observations: Unauthenticated public demo by design; abuse control is per-UTC-day and hourly usage caps enforced before any provider call, plus allowance holds (backend/app/services/allowance_holds.py, migrations 0007/0009/0010).
CORS is pinned to exactly one origin from settings.cors_origin, never '*' (backend/app/main.py).

Free-text inputs pass a moderation/text gate (services/moderation.py, services/text_gate.py); backend/app/api/embeddings.py documents the resulting privacy trade — visitor text that previously never left the process is now sent to a third-party moderation endpoint.
Render secrets are declared `sync: false` in render.yaml so they are entered in the dashboard rather than committed.
Browser localStorage holds theme preference only and is explicitly 'not a source of truth' (README.md).
other_notes: Monorepo with two build systems: uv/pyproject.toml at the repo root for the backend and npm/Vite in frontend/; configuration for both lives in one .env at the repo root.
Secondary frontend commands: `cd frontend && npm run test` (vitest run), `cd frontend && npm run lint` (oxlint), `cd frontend && npm run preview`.
Database migration invocation: `uv run alembic upgrade head` using backend/alembic.ini (11 revisions through 0011_moderation_log).

Render build command for the api service: `pip install uv && uv sync --frozen --no-dev && uv run python -c "...SentenceTransformer(...)"` — pre-downloads the ~88 MB embedding model at build time to avoid cold-start downloads and Hugging Face anonymous rate limits.
Render deploy targets: `bws4-api` (free Python web service, region oregon, rootDir '.') and a Render Static Site for the web client; render.yaml cites .spec4/v0/stack.json as their source.
No Dockerfile, docker-compose, Kubernetes/Helm manifests, or Terraform/Pulumi/CDK files are present.

Prompts are versioned Markdown files under each slice's prompts/ directory (writer_v1.md, critic_v1.md, answer_v1.md/answer_v2.md, delegation_v1.md, merge_v1.md, specialist_v1.md, planner_v1.md, research_v1.md, synthesis_v1.md, agent_v1.md), loaded by per-app prompt_loader.py modules.
Every source file opens with the marker comment `# Built with Spec4 AI - https://spec4.ai` (`//` in TypeScript).
Google-style docstrings are an explicit project convention, stated inline in backend/app/api/embeddings.py.
FastAPI Depends-based DI is used deliberately so tests can substitute dependencies via app.dependency_overrides (see get_db_session, get_embedder).
Streaming is wired end to end: sse-starlette on the backend, @microsoft/fetch-event-source in the browser.
`.python-version` file present at the repo root; `.env.example` present.

RAG corpus is 10 curated Markdown documents in backend/app/rag/dataset/ (space-exploration topics), chunked by a hand-rolled sentence-aligned overlapping-window pipeline and indexed into a dataset_embeddings table.
Golden-case evaluation fixtures exist for planning (backend/tests/golden/planning_cases.json) and orchestrated delegation/merge (backend/tests/orchestrated/golden/).
Repo governance files present: CLA.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CLAUDE.md, LICENSE.
backend/app/services/untrusted.py and backend/app/services/web_search.py (Exa) mark a deliberate boundary around untrusted third-party content.
